statement: Fossils from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco, previously estimated at roughly 40,000-160,000 years old, were redated in 2017 to 315 ± 34 thousand years ago via thermoluminescence dating of associated fire-heated flint artifacts (range approx. 349-281 ka at 1σ), cross-checked with electron spin resonance dating on a hominin tooth — making this the oldest well-dated Homo sapiens material at time of publication, roughly 100,000+ years older than the previous best-dated specimen (Omo Kibish).

sources.citation: Hublin, J.-J., Ben-Ncer, A., Bailey, S.E., et al. "New fossils from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco and the pan-African origin of Homo sapiens." Nature 546: 289-292. DOI: 10.1038/nature22336
sources.author: Hublin et al.

sources.citation: Richter, D., Grün, R., Joannes-Boyau, R., et al. "The age of the hominin fossils from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco, and the origins of the Middle Stone Age." Nature 546: 293-296. DOI: 10.1038/nature22335
sources.author: Richter et al.

notes: Report as "315 ± 34 ka," not a bare rounded "300,000" — the precision matters for the app’s no-false-precision principle.
